intro: Marble Rendix claims the analysis is handled by AI models, so newcomers can follow signals instead of charts. The claim is easy to publish. The verification is what this review looks for.

In practice it works like this: you register free, fund US$300, choose automatic or manual mode, and let the models propose entries across 9 assets while the practice account lets you learn without risk.
The checks below follow the platform published pages in order - what it claims, what the fine print says, and where the two diverge. The verdict is a summary of those checks, nothing more.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$300 minimum.

faqs.q: Is it really fee-free?
faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: Can I trade manually?
faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
The verdict holds at 4.5: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
